PRESIDENT'S PAGE
It is my privilege to
wholeheartedly endorse the most important
work which the Board of Trustees of the Psi Upsilon Foundation
are
carrying on to
stiengthen the competitive position of our fra
ternity.
The conti-ibution which this Foundation will make to the prog
ress and prosperity of Psi Upsilon will become apparent to all of
our brothers as the success of its endeavors becomes clear.
I, therefore, in my oflScial capacity, not only support this effort
but call upon our
membership to give prompt and generous con
sideration to it and to those who are
carrying the burden for us.
To my mind there are several unique and forceful reasons for aiding in this program.
To those of us who wish to render significant scholarship aid to carefully chosen recipients,
I know of no other way one can be so certain that his help will reach the character and
personahty of youth that assistance to the Psi Upsilon Foundation will oflFer. Surely his
membership in our
fraternity estabhshes a level to begin with and our own
Scholarship
Committee further screens the candidates.
These funds also wiU enable some of our most earnest and deserving men to continue
in college and finish their college courses who may otherwise find the burden too great.
As a
fraternity we should strongly support such an effort, particularly where it is
deserved.
We should also be in a
position, when funds become available, to encourage our more
gifted brothers to continue their education in graduate schools in order to place them in
the most strategic educated position to compete with the highest talent in the country with
success and thus bring honors in life not only to themselves but to Psi U as well.
Now that we have secured the necessary approval from the U. S. Internal Revenue
Service that gifts made to our Foundation are deductible without question from gross
income before figuring income taxes within the limits of the code, I believe we are now
ready to move ahead more
rapidly to obtain our ends.
I can assure our membership that the able committees appointed to make awards on
the one hand and to handle the investment of the Endowment Funds on the other hand,
are
composed of dedicated men of experience specially chosen to
carry out their respec
tive responsibihties on a careful and conservative basis.
I sincerely wish to add my deep appreciation to all those who are
contributing time,
eflFort and worldly goods to make this organization the successful and helpful arm of
Psi Upsilon. which I know it is about to become.
Robert W. Parsons, Xi '22

OUR FOUNDATION
By R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15
President The Psi Upsilon Foundation, Inc.
R. Bourke Corcoran
We have all heard "MR. PSI UPSI
LON," Earl D. Babst, Iota-Phi '93, say:
"Psi Upsilon is a
living brotherhood
founded on romance and tradition. It is
nourished by sentiment."
The truly great U. S. Senator (18811905) from Connecticut, Joseph R. Hawley, Psi 1847, wrote shortly before he died:
"The fitness and capacity for friend
ship, and the ability to attract and re
tain true friends, are as well subject to
cultivation and improvement as
any
quality or
power of mind, and the cul
tivation bears rich and precious fruit in
the maturity and old age of man. In
this culture lies one of the chief values
of our eminent and beloved Psi Upsilon
brotherhood."
CHALLENGE OF THE FUTURE
Since its founding in 1833, Psi Upsilon
has met the opportunity of the hour and
accepted the chaUenge of the future. Few
organizations can look back through such
a
long, unbroken corridor of time and
find it illuminated by the brilliant achieve
ments of so
many wearers of our
Badge of
Brotherhood: men of distinction in all
walks of life�the highest echelons of gov
ernment, the courts, the church, educa
tion, arts, science and all phases of in
dustry�men who have played and are
playing major parts in molding and shap
ing the greatness of this continent. It has
given the nation many thousands of citi
zens
sincerely devoted in their dedication
to the public weal. Psi Upsilon exem
plifies the responsible citizenship and com
munity leadership which recognize their
duty of participating in the building of
the nation's future.
Psi Upsilon has been distinguished in
its eflForts to encourage high standards of
scholarship and particularly in the devel
opment of responsible citizens of high
moral standards.
These, then were
among the reflections
of a
group of Psi Upsilon men who met
in a series of discussions of how to im
plement the realization that in this es
pecially critical time there offered a
major
opportunity for another practical demon
stration of the Psi Upsilon spirit of the
helping hand.
WE HOPE FOR yOUR
PARTICIPATION
The Psi Upsilon Foundation, Inc., is
the culmination of many years of effort by
the Fraternity to create an educational
foundation through which members of Psi
Upsilon can contribute to the permanent
welfare of the Fraternity and which will
meet the requirements of Section 501 (c)
(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954.
This section of the Code provides that
organizations which meet its requirement
shall be exempt from income tax. Contri
butions to such organizations are deducti
ble by the donor for income, estate and
gift tax purposes. The purposes of the
Foundation, as
expressed in the Articles
of Incorporation, were drawn to meet these
specifications.

4 THE DIAMOND OF PSI EPSILON
Final ruhng has been issued by the In
ternal Revenue Service to the Founda
tion.
The Foundation, conceived and admin
istered by business and professional men
who are members of the Psi Upsilon Fra
ternity, was estabhshed to enable the
18,000 living members of the Fraternity
to join in a
program that well may be
come the most noteworthy of the fine
projects with which the name of Psi Upsi
lon has been associated throughout its il
lustrious one hundred and thirty years.
The Psi Upsilon Foundation, Inc., is a
thoughtfully developed enterprise created
to perform an
important function in the
field of higher education. To achieve its
purposes, it seeks contributions of money,
securities and real property. The income
of its working fund wiU be used primarily
to aid deserving undergraduates and grad
uate students in colleges, universities and
other institutions of higher learning and
for associated purposes.
NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATION
This is a NON-PROFIT organization.
Its income MUST be used EXCLUSIVE
LY for the purposes stated in the Articles
of Incorporation, as outlined in this bro^
chure. There will be no accumulation of
income from any property held by the
corporation. Whatever income is received
will be expended within the year in which
it is received, or as soon thereafter as is
practicable. The income will be kept in
motion. While the principal fund may be
used legally for the declared purposes of
the Foundation, it is a basic policy to re
tain intact this principal, disbursing only
the income.
The Manufacturers Hanover Trust Com
pany of New York are Custodian of the
funds of the Foundation.
CAPITAL and INCOME
All gifts to the Foundation go to our
Capital account. Income from this Capital
account is used for our
scholarships.
FINANCE COMMIHEE
The Finance Committee of the Founda
tion consists of Brother Benjamin T. Bur
ton, Chi '21, Robert W. Parsons, Xi '22
and Edward S. Fries, Eta '45, all excep
tionally well qualified by years of experi
ence to handle this most important task
of our
responsibility. Their actions are, of
course, subject to the authorization or
ap
proval of the entire Board of Directors.
At an
early date when our
Capital fund
is somewhat larger, we intend to have one
of the major banks of New York City act
as our investment advisor.
Copies of the final approval by
the U. S. Internal Revenue Service
are available at our
headquarters.
CANADA
Arrangements are
practically completed
for the establishment of a Psi Upsilon
Foundation, Ltd. in Canada. The Canadian
government revenue service has approved
of their apphcation for the exemption, sim
ilar to ours in the United States. One of
the U. S. Board of Directors will be a
member of the Canadian Foundation Board
so as to coordinate our efforts.
The Psi Upsilon Foundation, Inc.

PSI UPSILON FOUNDATION GRANTS
By Laurance G. Wolfe, Rho '38
Alumni Editor, Diamond of Psi Upsilon
"You may rest assured that I will con
tinue to make every effort in behalf of
the University, the chapter, and my own
academic progress."
These words, from an
undergraduate
brother's letter acknowledging a Psi U
Foundation grant, have important signifi
cance. For they reflect the seriousness of
purpose which is characteristic of the
young men who seek and receive scholar
ship awards from our
fledgling Founda
tion.
A glimpse at the letters from those who
have won Psi U Foundation grants pro
vides rewarding moments to those who are
convinced that our
younger Psi U's are
preparing for tomorrow's leadership re
sponsibilities.
"It is a
great honor to he chosen as a
recipient of a Psi Upsilon Foundation
grant," writes one brother. "I wish to ex
press my deepest appreciation for this op
portunity to take full advantage of my
educational experiences and to assure
you
that my pride is shared by my chapter
brothers."
Often the grant-winning brother will
refer to the need which stimulated his
application for assistance from the Founda
tion: "This money will be most helpful in
meeting my college expenses for next
year," wrote an award-winner. "I appre
ciate the interest of . . .
(the Foundation)
. . . in undergraduate brothers, as I am
sure others do who have received grants
from the Foundation."
Another writes�"Were it not for the
Foundation grant I would not have been
able to complete the semester even with
a loan of $200 from the University . . .
with your aid I am able to meet all ob
ligations. . . ."
StiU another writer�this one in his letter
of apphcation�"Wii/i . . .
(a grant) . . .
from the Foundation I will be able to keep
living in the chapter house. . . ."
The Foundation is still too young to
have bulging files of letters such as those
quoted here. There is a
thank-you note
from each of the brothers who have been
awarded scholarship aid. All the letters,
in one
way or another, offer the thought
expressed by one brother in a
closing para
graph which reads:
"I hope someday in the future to assist
the Foundation in their efforts to help
other Brothers."
All members of Psi Upsilon must be
encouraged by the way the Psi Upsilon
Foundation is growing. The reaction of
those who have earned Foundation awards
to date certainly is conducive to such en
couragement.
The deepest satisfaction, to be sure,
must be felt by those whose contributions
to the Foundation have put it in the busi
ness of "helping other Brothers."

WHO IS R. BOURKE CORCORAN?
R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15, has
been identified with many of the major
developments that have kept Psi Upsilon
in the forefront of the fraternity world.
The same zeal, spirit and dedication which
brought him election to the Executive
Council of the Fraternity in 1920, have
continued to permeate all the Psi U proj
ects in the ensuing years with which he
has been associated. It is indeed fitting
that the Psi Upsilon Foundation, Inc.
should call on Bourke Corcoran's genius
for organization and his unselfish and sin
cere concern for his Brothers in Psi U.
Brother Corcoran's retirement from an
active business career has enabled the Fra
temity to utilize fuU-time his many qual
ifications. He has served as General Chair
man of the fund-raising drive for the Psi
Upsilon Foundation, Inc. since its incep
tion in 1959. He was elected President
and a Director of the Foundation in Octo
ber, 1962.
Bourke Corcoran has given over 50
years of devoted service to Psi U. Even
before his election to Council in 1920,
Brother Corcoran had served as a
delegate
to two conventions� 1914 and 1918.
The prime mover in the revival of The
Diamond in 1920, he was its business
manager for three years and served as its
editor and a member of the Executive
Council's Committee on The Diamond
until November, 1934. The successful im
plementation of a Life Subscription Fund
to endow this publication as a forum for
recording the hving history of the Frater
nity was a
major accomplishment during
this period. Brother Corcoran contributed
the chapter on the history of The Dia
mond, "the first college fraternity maga
zine," for the Annals of Psi Upsilon. With
his return to the Executive Council in
1959, he once
again became chairman of
the Executive Council's committee for the
publication of The Diamond.
Brother Corcoran's service on the Exec
utive Council has been varied and' out
standing. He was
Secretary from 19301933. Brother Edward L. Stevens, Chi '99,
in his address at the Fraternity's centen
nial in 1933 made the following evalua
tion of Bourke Corcoran's contribution to
Psi U: "Any man who can revive a
dying
business every month or two, as a voca
tion, and, on the side, runs a
Fraternity's
correspondence, dinners, magazine and
mailing list, to say nothing of visiting half
a dozen or more
Chapters each year (with
a few Phi Beta Kappa keys in one
pocket
and the wrath of God in the other) still
has marrow in his bones." Brother Cor
coran was
vice-president of Council from
1937-1940. He returned to Council in
1959 when he was elected an
Honorary
Life Member.
Brother Corcoran's numerous other con
tributions to Psi U includes service as
Fraternity Archivist 1928-1929; supervis
ing the production of the 906-page Direc
tory of the Fraternity, pubhshed in 1931;
assisting Brother Earl D. Babst, Iota-Phi
'93, in setting up the program for the in
stallation of the Epsilon Phi Chapter in
1928; and co-author of the History of the
Omega Chapter with Floyd Stauffer,
Omega '37, in 1941. The renovation of
the headquarters and archives of the Fra
ternity in 1960 were also carried out under
Brother Corcoran's direction.
Brother Corcoran's business activity until
his retirement a few years ago was
equal
ly varied and challenging. After several
years with the General Electric Company
he became an account representative at
J. Walter Thompson Company. He then
became an official of the newly formed
National Electrical Manufacturers Asso
ciation. He retired in 1958 after years of
service as head of the Chicago ofiice of
the Picker X-Ray Corporation.
More important than a strict factual
accounting of Bourke Corcoran's accom
plishments, are the countless occasions
when he has given invaluable behind the
scenes counsel and aid to many under
graduate and alumni brothers over the
years. It is this kind of dedication and
ability to get things done that have made
Bourke Corcoran once
again "the Psi U
man of the hour."�H. C. C.

Gifts of securities or property
Every donor, whether he gives modestly or
substantially, can save
money, or
give
more
generously at the same cost, by giving securities which have increased in value
since purchase rather than cash. The increase in value is not subject to capital gains
tax; the market value of the securities at the time of the gift measures the amount
which is deductible, subject to federal and state tax law limitations. The fact that
your securities may be more than the exact denomination you wish to give makes no
difference. Simply send your certificate to the Treasurer with instructions as to the
number of shares you wish returned. The Foundation wiU send you a new certificate
for those shares.
Gifts of real property offer the same
general advantages as
gffts of securities.
There are added advantages if such property consists of business real estate on
which depreciation has been taken. The gift can be spread over a
period of years, if
necessary, to secure maximum gift deduction. If it is not obliged to keep or main
tain the property, the Foundation, under many circumstances, is prepared to accept
gifts of real property. Before making such a
gift, the prospective donor should con
sult the Foundation.
